The Same-Day Agent Survival Proof already landed at commit `84e5b4f719f56843d4562bf38a129ceedabfbcd8`. Bernays did not mint a competing SKU or alter its USD 2,500 price.

This extension closes the operational gaps around that offer: a deterministic failure/recovery canary with a production-survival receipt schema, one binary acceptance test locked before invoicing, pain-triggered outreach and follow-ups, marketplace order, claims guardrails, and a mapping to the existing Airtable Revenue Pipeline with no second CRM or table.

The canary forces a timeout after an external effect but before the completion checkpoint. Recovery reuses the same idempotency key; the receipt must show two attempts, one dedupe hit, one external effect, and `DONE`. Replay must leave those facts unchanged.

The delivery clock starts only at the agreed America/New_York window after a customer-specific hosted invoice has provider-confirmed authorization. If the exact binary test misses `window_end`, refund follows unless the buyer elects one free next-business-day repair attempt. Commons stores no private processor data.

The existing $12,000 GGUF diagnostic, $30,000 White Box engagement, Subzero, human-outcomes, DIO, portfolio_overdrive, and pixel pack remain unchanged. The independent seven-contact GGUF transport also remains independent and deduped.
